evals.prompt: hey i just installed this design twin plugin in claude code, what does it actually do and how do i get claude talking to my figma file?
evals.expected_output: Explains both connection modes (dtwin CLI, figma-mcp server), what each lets Claude do, and the short steps to open a connection (plugin running in Figma, then pick CLI or MCP). Hands off to /designtwin:help for setup details and /designtwin:extract for actually pulling data, without reciting the full flag/tool reference inline.
expectations: Mentions the dtwin CLI as one way to connect
Mentions the figma-mcp / MCP server as the other way to connect
States the Figma file must be open with the plugin running (not headless)
Names at least one concrete next step to actually open a connection (e.g. import the plugin, run dtwin --list, register .mcp.json)
Points to /designtwin:extract and/or /designtwin:help for next steps rather than reciting the full CLI flag or MCP tool reference inline
Does not fabricate commands, flags, or tool names that don't exist in the repo (dtwin flags, figma_* tool names)

evals.prompt: is there a way for claude to just read my figma file directly instead of me exporting stuff manually?
evals.expected_output: Identifies this as answered by the CLI/MCP connection (not manual export), briefly contrasts the CLI (one-shot/daemon, read-only, writes to design/) vs MCP (live, interactive, in-conversation), and gives the short path to get one running.
expectations: Answers yes and points at the CLI and/or MCP connection as the direct-read alternative to manual export
Distinguishes the CLI (writes files to design/, one-shot or daemon) from the MCP server (live, interactive tool calls)
States the Figma file must be open with the plugin running
Gives a concrete first action rather than only describing concepts abstractly
Does not claim this works headlessly or without the Figma desktop plugin running

evals.prompt: what's this figma-mcp thing i see in the bridge folder, do i need it?
evals.expected_output: Explains figma-mcp is the live/interactive MCP connection (vs the dtwin CLI's one-shot/bulk reads), that it's optional (not required for the CLI path), what it lets Claude do (live tool calls, figma_export_url for pasted links, safe writes), and how it gets registered (in the consuming project, not this repo).
expectations: Correctly identifies figma-mcp as the MCP server / interactive connection, distinct from the dtwin CLI
States it is optional — the CLI path works without it
Mentions it needs to be registered (.mcp.json) in the project being built, not in this repo
Mentions at least one concrete capability it adds (live queries, pasting a Figma link, or safe writes)
Does not claim the MCP server is required to use Design Twin at all
